messages:
Mira: Ran a cross-region mini-sweep this morning comparing L4 / T4 / A10G for embeddings and small-chat workloads. Focused on p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, and cost per 1M tokens. Posting the quick raw summary and notes below.

Devon: nice — can you paste the numbers and config?

bench-bot: sweep complete (run id: sweep-1990001)
```
region | gpu  | workload    | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | tok/s | 1M-token-cost($)
-------|------|-------------|---------|---------|-------|-----------------
us-west| A10G | small-chat  | 42      | 128     | 850   | 24.1
us-west| L4   | small-chat  | 58      | 190     | 420   | 12.5
us-west| T4   | small-chat  | 95      | 360     | 200   | 7.8
eu-cent| L4   | embeddings  | 12      | 28      | 2500  | 4.2
eu-cent| T4   | embeddings  | 18      | 50      | 1400  | 3.6
apac   | A10G | embeddings  | 14      | 35      | 2300  | 12.0
```
(quant: q4_1 / L4=q4_1, T4=fp16, A10G=bfloat16 default; batch sizes tuned per region)

Sanjay: quick takeaways — A10G gives best small-chat throughput and tail latency in us-west but cost per million tokens is much higher. L4 hits a sweet spot for embeddings cost-per-unit in eu-central. T4 is the cheapest raw GPU-hour but loses badly on latency for small-chat (higher client-visible p95).

Cassidy: which kernels were used for the runs? cuBLAS vs our fused kernels? Any custom kernels enabled?

Mira: Kernel details: L4 runs used our fused_attention + kv-cache optimized path (fused_kv_v2) with int8 q4_1; T4 used cutlass fp16 kernels and the generic attention path; A10G used cuBLAS/TF32 path with the new matmul-tiling fallback disabled. Canary config snippet: 
```
{"model":"small-chat-v2","quant":"q4_1","kernel_overrides":["fused_kv_v2"],"auto_batch":true}
```
Note: that JSON is just the canary config we applied to the runtime, not the full job metadata.

Devon: any quality regressions from quantization, esp. small-chat replies?

Mira: Slight drop on small-chat for q4_1 in L4 — measured on our 1k-sample eval set: METEOR -0.4, BLEU -0.6 absolute. For embeddings the cosine similarity against fp16 baseline is ~0.998 median, so safe. For small-chat we saw edge cases on numeric precision (dates, small arithmetic). I pushed a prompt-level mitigation that reduces generation temperature for those cases — helps but not perfect.

Sanjay: capacity sizing notes: to sustain 1k rps embeddings (avg req = 1k tokens) in eu-central we estimate: L4 ~8 GPUs, T4 ~12 GPUs, A10G ~6 GPUs (A10G higher throughput but you pay more per GPU). For small-chat 200 rps (avg 80 tokens) in us-west, A10G cluster of 4 gives ~headroom, L4 needs 8, T4 needs 14 (very rough, includes autoscale padding).

Cassidy: any regional anomalies? APAC A10G had higher p95 on small-chat in one run — cause?

Mira: APAC noise traced to noisy PCIe link on the instance type we used (scheduling to a different host fixed it). Also noticed different kernel selection heuristics in our scheduler by region (we fallback to cutlass on older AMIs). We're going to standardize the AMI/kernel mapping to reduce variance.

bench-bot: uploaded artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/sweep-1990001/ (profiles, flamegraphs, logs)

Devon: next steps?

Mira: 1) open a small canary for fused_kv rollout in eu for embeddings (24h). 2) run a targeted quant A/B for small-chat with q4_1 vs q8_0 on L4 to measure quality vs cost. 3) update scheduler to prefer fused_kv on newer AMIs. I'll create RFC/PRs for the above after lunch.

Cassidy: yup +1. Throw up the canary tags and I'll watch the eval dashboards. :eyes:

Sanjay: If canary looks good we should prepare a Dedicated capacity quote (estimates attached in artifacts) and loop in sales.

Mira: cool — thanks all. Filing the follow-ups now. :rocket:
